title: Vintage Cinnamon Rolls
creator: O'Leary, Betty
description: This object is a recipe that was created by Betty O'Leary when she work for Orion High School in Orion, Illinois as a cafeteria worker. The recipe was later modified by Lisa O'Leary-Volk, who wrote the current recipe on the object. The original recipe was damaged after years of use.
subject: United States--Social life and customs--Miscellanea.; Formulas, recipes, etc.--History.; Comfort food--Recipes.
ingredient: 1/2c Warm Water; 2 Packets of Dry Quick Yeast; 1 1/2c Scalded Milk; 1/2c Sugar; 1tsp Salt; 2 Eggs (Slightly Beaten); 1/2c Crisco; 4c Flour; 4tbsp Melted Butter; 3/4c Brown Sugar; 2tsp Cinnamon; 1c Powdered Sugar; 1c Powdered Sugar; 1tbsp Milk;  1/2tsp Vanilla
directions: Dissolve yeast in warm water, cool milk to lukewarm, and add to the yeast water.; Add all other ingrediets to the liquid and mix until you can handle dought (dough should not be stiff).; Place dough in oiled bowl and cover with a damp cloth to rise and double in size. Preheat oven to 375 degrees.; Punch the dough down and roll out on floured surface. Brush with melted butter, and sprinkle brown sugar and cinnamon mixture on rolled out dough.; Pull dough tight and work into a roll (roll out in half) place both halves on cookie sheet (cover and let rise until doubled).; Once risen, cut rolls in desired thickness, approximately three inches.; Place on cookie sheets and bake at 370 degrees for 20-25 minutes. Frost while warm with the powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla.

title: Chocolate Chip Scones
creator: Rochford-Volk, Jake
description: This object is a recipe from Jake Rochford-Volk woho experiemented with creating scones based on a few different bread recipes. The text of this recipe was written by Nolan Rochford-Volk based on the original, which was damaged after excessive rewrites while perfecting the recipe.

ingredient: 3c All-purpose Flour; 1/2c Granulated Sugar; 1/2c Lightly Packed Brown Sugar; 1 1/8tsp Fine Sea Salt; 1tbsp Baking Powder; 1tsp Baking Soda; 1 10oz Bag of Mini Semi-sweek Chocolate Chips; 1 1/2 Sticks, Unsalted Butter (cold and cubed); 1c Buttermilk (cold); 2 Eggs; 2tsp Vanilla; Coarse Sugar for Topping
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. In a large bowl, combine flour, sugars, salt, baking powder, baking soda, and chocolate chips. Add the butter and cut with a fork until butter is pea-sized.; In a separate bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, 1 egg, and vanilla extract.; Make a well in the middle of the dry mix and liquid mix.; Mix until combined, but don't overmix.; Transfer dough to a floured surface. Shape into rectangle. Fold in half like a piece of paper. Flatten into a rectagle. Fold in half again but in the opposite direction. Gently press dought into a 1 1/2 inch tall round.; Divide into two equal parts.; Cut each part into six wedges and place two-inches apart. If dough is warm, freeze for 10-20 minutes.; In a small bowl, combine 1 egg with 1tsp water. Brush over scones and sprinkle with sugar.; Bake for 18-20 minutes or unitl lightly browned. Allow to sit for 30-60 minutes before serving. Store in an airtight container for up to three days.
